title: The Completely Free Video to 3D Gaussian Splatting Pipeline - YouTube

snippets.text: This is a completely free open-source
pipeline that will allow you to train
Gaussian splats from video inputs in
three steps. As an example, we'll be
transforming this video and converting
it into a Gaussian splat. Now, you might
have seen other examples of research,
but you won't need to know all of these
mathematics. You won't need a degree in
computer science. These individual
[music] points, instead of pixels, are
made up of three-dimensional voxels,
roughly in the shape of an oval.
This pipeline consists of three distinct
steps. First step is frame extraction,
which extracts individual frames from
your video. Second is [music] structure
from motion, which detects features on
individual frames of the video and looks
for how your camera moved through the
scene. For these first two steps, we'll
be using RealityCapture from Unreal
Engine. The third step is Gaussian
training. Gaussian training takes the
structure from motion files from
RealityCapture and trains the individual
3D point cloud into a 3D reconstruction.
Almost like a model that you can
navigate around from [music] any angle.
This third step will be done using a
free open-source software called Brush,
which is available on GitHub. All of
these links, these downloads, will
[music] be linked in the description.
